content.comment_body: Hello, I'm new to IoT services and cloud communications. I'm trying to connect my [product_name] [version_no] with a cloud service called ThingsBoard. I successfully published data to ThingsBoard using MQTT protocol on port 1883. However, I need to add more security to our projects and now I'm attempting MQTTS/TLS communication with one-way verification, using a CA certificate generated by the ThingsBoard broker over port 8883. Unfortunately, I'm unable to establish this connection between my [product_name] and the cloud service. I tested communication on my computer using an app called MQTTX and it worked fine. I was also able to set up MQTTS/TLS connections with [product_name] before, via port 443 and some network redirections. My guess is that the limited choice of ports or the way the broker URL prefix needs to switch from "mqtt://brokerurl" to "mqtts://brokerurl" might be causing the problem. Any advice would be helpful; I've tried many approaches and checked every manual available. I've attached screenshots of my [product_name] settings and ThingsBoard credentials. Thanks in advance.
I'm facing the same issue and cannot connect my [product_name] [version_no] with updated firmware to an MQTTS broker. MQTT works without issues. Have you found a solution? Thanks.
Hello, according to the information in the [product_name] [version_no] manual, MQTTS is not supported. Please review chapter 11 in the manual.
Could you indicate where in Chapter 11 it states that connection via MQTTS is not possible? Thank you.
The manual does not mention MQTTS at all, it only refers to MQTT.
As mentioned previously, MQTTS is not listed. The [product_name] only supports features included in the manual.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering difficulty establishing secure MQTTS/TLS connections between their [product_name] [version_no] and a cloud service, while basic MQTT connectivity works. There is uncertainty regarding MQTTS/TLS support, and searches through documentation have not clarified this, leading to frustration about unclear documentation and perceived lack of security features.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect their [product_name] [version_no] to provide secure MQTTS/TLS communication with external cloud brokers, including options for custom CA certificates and broker URLs, similar to the flexibility found in standard MQTT or third-party client applications.
